IncidentBot: PAGER | P1 | elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate — region eu-west1 experiencing spike, smart-routing started regional fallbacks
Alice M.: on it, looking at routing logs now. any customer reports?
Ben (oncall): getting reports from two enterprise customers in eu region, spikes started ~09:42 UTC 
SRE Pager: metrics: 5xx rate went from 0.2% -> 6.8% across eu-west1 within 4m. latency increased 3x.
Alice M.: smart-routing shows fallback policy picking model-variant "rw-infer-small-q4" due to queue depth, but that variant has different kernel and is timing out on certain sequence lengths.
Ben (oncall): we tried a quick manual pin to the larger variant to stop the fallback. command I ran:```bash
redwoodctl routing override --scope=eu-west1 --model=rw-infer-large --reason="mitigate timeouts"
```
Charlie: got that. after the override, errors dropped briefly then started increasing and we saw traffic shift to us-west1. looks like cross-region spillover and region saturation.
Dana: ah — autoscaling in eu-west1 couldn't reclaim capacity because pinned variant consumes more GPU mem -> eviction of queued tasks -> retrying clients to next region -> loop.
Ben (oncall): ack, that'd explain the cascade. I rolled the override back:```bash
redwoodctl routing clear-override --scope=eu-west1
```
Alice M.: roll back confirmed, but we still have degraded tail latency while kv-cache warms. many requests still being routed to fallback variants by policy; need graceful fallback not abrupt pin/clear.
SRE Pager: customer impact: 2 tenants saw >20% error rate for 12m, several more had latency P95 > 2s. flagging for CS comms.
OpsBot: Incident channel created: #incidents/1812345678. Slack paging initiated.
Charlie: handing over to me for triage, Ben you can rest. I'm clustering logs now.
Ben (oncall): thanks, Charlie — leaving a note in the incident doc. please escalate if you need escalation to infra.
Charlie: grep of routing logs shows a weird loop: requests that failed in eu-west1 were retried immediately and smart-routing had a policy that prefers lower-cost variant in next region, but that variant had a mismatch tag and was incompatible for >1024 tokens -> immediate 500.
Dana: that's a policy mismatch between "compatible_variants" and the cross-region migration rules. operator override bypassed compatibility checks, which caused resource pressure.
Alice M.: good catch. we should add a guard to prevent manual override from selecting incompatible variants when region fallback is active.
Charlie: mitigation plan: 1) set temporary routing throttle to limit cross-region failover:```bash
redwoodctl routing set-policy --name=eu-fallback-throttle --max-cross-region-rt=2
```2) force a soft-failback to a warm, compatible variant instead of instant pin.
SRE Pager: applied throttle, seeing immediate drop in cross-region traffic. 5xx rate declining.
IncidentBot: NOTE: scheduled on-call handoff in 20m — Charlie -> Alice.
Charlie: starting handoff notes -> we reduced cross-region retries, cleared the hard override, and applied throttle. still waiting for KV cache to warm; recommend leave throttle for 30m.
Alice M.: taking over. I'm going to coordinate postmortem and customer comms. @dana can you draft impact blurb for CS?
Dana: on it — draft: "We experienced an elevated error rate affecting generation calls in EU region due to a routing policy mismatch and a subsequent manual override that increased cross-region retries. We mitigated by throttling cross-region failovers and restoring compatible fallback behavior."
Charlie: FYI — one enterprise had manual retries from their client; recommend CS call checklist: advise clients to backoff and don't retry immediately.
Ben (oncall): small note — my override command didn't warn about compatibility; maybe redwoodctl should prompt when override changes model family across regions.
SRE Pager: agree, add guard rails: require `--force` if compatibility check fails and log an explicit audit event.
Alice M.: adding action items now: 1) temporary: keep fallback throttle for 30m, monitor. 2) post-incident: add compatibility checks on overrides, add dry-run for overrides, improve fallback to prefer warm variants. 3) product: document manual-override risks and runbook update.
Charlie: capturing logs and traces in incident doc: link -> https://redwood.internal/incidents/1812345678 (internal)
IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE | status: mitigating | assigned: Charlie -> Alice | severity: P1 | impact: partial region degradation | ETA next update: 15m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Alice M.: thanks everyone — brief customer notice scheduled in 10m targeting impacted tenants. I'll post final update after throttle period.
Dana: postmortem owner volunteer: @Dana, can run the follow-up and include root-cause analysis, timeline, and changes.
Ben (oncall): closing note: for future emergency manual steps, prefer `redwoodctl routing suggested-fallback --dry-run` to see compatibility and estimated mem usage.
Alice M.: agreed — we should make dry-run the default unless `--unsafe` is passed.
SRE Pager: 5xx rate back down to baseline, latency improving. marking incident as mitigated for now, leaving P1 until postmortem completed. :white_check_mark:
